pack.title: A king puts Dublin on silver

presentation.anchor: Sihtric Silkbeard · Dublin mint · silver penny
presentation.question: Whose name and authority travel with the silver?
presentation.opening: A small silver penny makes the port, ruler and a wider trading world tangible.
presentation.evidenceLimit: A coin can show names, design choices and a minting economy. It cannot prove one motive for founding the mint.
presentation.sourceDetail: Learner-facing specimen remains to be selected
presentation.artifactPrompt: Keep a personal mark separate from the historical penny.
presentation.tegCanDo: Use familiar words for movement and exchange.

pages.title: The port before the penny
pages.body: The coin enters a connected port and market already moving people, goods and silver.

pages.title: Two names hold the city
pages.body: The modern city carries both Irish place-name histories without collapsing them into one origin story.

pages.title: Small object, large claim
pages.body: Under Sihtric, Dublin produced the first locally struck Irish coinage known to numismatists.
pages.detail: The date remains a range rather than one theatrical minting day.

pages.title: Read the object honestly
pages.body: Separate what a coin can show from what historians infer.

exercise.objective: Keep a material coin claim separate from unsupported motive.
exercise.prompt: What can a selected penny directly show?
exercise.answer: A name and coin design struck in silver.

options.text: A name and coin design struck in silver.
options.rationale: The object can directly preserve these features.
The coin alone cannot establish universal motive or response.

options.text: The exact day the mint opened.
options.rationale: The evidence supports a date range.

exercise.hint: Choose what can remain visible on the object.
exercise.recovery: That answer needs evidence beyond the coin itself.

pages.title: Name and city travel
pages.body: A suitable example can carry ruler and place beyond the mint. Final copy waits for one specialist-approved specimen and reading.
